quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug that affects your ability to drive safely. The law applies to all drugs—illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This creates space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Do not drive through the water. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the water. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. Even shallow water can hide hazards. If you see a flooded area, turn around and choose a different route.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet roads, the less your tires can grip the surface. If you go too fast, your tires may lose contact with the road and hydroplane—sliding on a layer of water.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, steer your wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: During a skid, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle starts to straighten out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed.
questions.explanation: When being passed, maintain your speed and do not accelerate. Let the other driver safely return to your lane.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Stay calm during a blowout. Hold the steering wheel firmly and remove your foot from the accelerator. Gently apply the brakes once the vehicle has slowed down. Do not move to the shoulder until your car has slowed significantly.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street to:

options.text: Account for stopping distance on the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: See potential hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch ahead for changes in traffic. Look for signals from other drivers. Be ready for vehicles entering at on-ramps and be prepared for sudden changes in road conditions and traffic.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and the vehicle slides on a film of water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle that just parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Assume the driver will open the car door as you approach.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver will open the car door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked vehicle, assume the driver will open the door as you approach. Use extra caution when driving near parked cars.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross because trains rarely come.
Safe places to park your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Always look and listen for trains coming from either direction. Follow all signs, signals, and directions from flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or when they do something unexpected. Talk to other drivers using signals to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. You should:

options.text: Leave because you did all you can.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: When you hit a parked car, stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing is ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn about dangers or special conditions ahead. Round signs are used only to warn about railroad crossings.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway begins ahead. Stay to the right of the median divider.

questions.question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice:

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, use a low gear before going down steep hills. Follow farther behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid sudden stops. Unless you have antilock brakes, pump the brakes to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.correctAnswerText: In the shade.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be extra careful on shaded roads near trees or buildings. These areas freeze before other parts of the road and are the last places to dry.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, looking far ahead helps you:
questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden braking or swerving.
questions.explanation: To avoid sudden braking or swerving, watch the road far ahead. By looking ahead and being ready to stop or change lanes, you can drive safely, use less fuel, and help traffic flow smoothly.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road edge, you should:

options.text: Slow down and gradually steer back onto the road when safe.
Turn back onto the road right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and gradually steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop off the road, do not turn back immediately. Slow down, check traffic, and gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: From top to bottom, what is the correct order of colors on a traffic light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights are always ordered the same way from top to bottom: red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line down the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: You are on a two-way road.
You are on a one-way road.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a two-way road.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass other vehicles when it is safe.

questions.question: How can you help the driver behind you stay at a safe distance?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Driving at a steady speed helps the driver behind you maintain a safe distance. Also signal your turns, lane changes, and slowing down.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow, how can you help other drivers see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers may have trouble seeing you. Use low beam headlights if you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: Your view is blocked at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.
questions.explanation: Always slow down at intersections. If you cannot see cross traffic clearly, stop completely. Then move forward slowly until you can see in both directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean stop. You must come to a complete stop and let other traffic go first. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: How can you see vehicles in your blind spots?
questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas your mirrors cannot show. Look over your shoulders to check for vehicles in these areas.

questions.question: What lights should you use in rain or fog to improve visibility?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. They help other drivers see you, even if they do not help you see much better.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you of hazards ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: When should you use your turn signals when parking at a curb?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
Only when pulling next to the curb.
When pulling next to the curb and when pulling away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to the curb and when pulling away from it.
questions.explanation: Always signal before pulling next to a curb and before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal to show other drivers your plan.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers you are changing lanes. Look for other drivers who may also be moving into your lane.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear its siren, you must pull over to the right side of the road right away and stop.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before going.
May drive through if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you may drive through the intersection if it is clear. You may also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This circular sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Watch for trains approaching the crossing.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are going. They may be moving faster than they appear. Always make sure you have enough space to safely change lanes before passing. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait to pass until it has gone by and you have plenty of room.

questions.question: You park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking facing downhill on any road, or facing uphill on a road without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way your car will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center so your car rolls into the curb if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Compared to daytime driving, night driving is:
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than daytime driving. It is harder to see in the dark. Headlights from other cars can blind you. There may be more tired or impaired drivers on the road at night.

questions.question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors for nearby traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for nearby traffic.
questions.explanation: When stopping on the road, check your mirrors first for traffic around you. Be aware of other drivers as you release the gas and let your car slow down. Then move to the brake pedal and press it smoothly to stop.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. A car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when standing water is on the road. Up to 35 mph, most tires push water away from the tire. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move water as well. Your tires may lose grip with the road and slide on the water like water skis.

questions.question: If the traffic light is red and you want to turn right, when can you turn?

options.text: When the cross traffic has cleared.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You may turn right at a red light after you stop completely, unless a sign says you cannot. Before you turn, you must let other traffic, pedestrians, and cyclists pass.

questions.question: When stopped at a red light with a green arrow showing, when may you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: First come to a complete stop.
Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You may proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear. You must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: For the first nine months that a driver under 18 has a probationary license, there are restrictions on:

options.text: The type and number of passengers that may be in their car.
Their purpose for driving between midnight and 5:00 a.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: For the first nine months, drivers under 18 can drive alone from 5:00 a.m. to midnight. Between midnight and 5:00 a.m., they can only drive alone if going to or from home, school, or work. There are also limits on how many passengers they can have at any time.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: If another driver is tailgating you, create more space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid a collision. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: What happens when a driver drives much slower than the speed limit?

options.text: It is a very safe way to drive.
The driver always has the right-of-way.
The driver should not let following cars pass.
It may create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be hazardous. On a two-lane road, if traffic backs up behind you because you are driving very slowly, you must pull over and let other vehicles pass.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all four corners, yield the right-of-way to any driver:
questions.correctAnswerText: Who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: After you stop, vehicles should go through a four-way stop in the order they arrived. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street with no emergency lights or siren on. What should you do?

options.text: Stop as quickly as you can.
Speed up to get out of its way.
Slow down, move far to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is following you but has no siren or flashing lights on, you do not need to move. Continue driving normally.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve.
Drive at least 35 mph around the curve.
Slow to 35 mph or less for the upcoming curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to 35 mph or less for the upcoming curve.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead. A speed advisory sign tells you the safe speed to drive for that section.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast for conditions causes many crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.
